claims.claim: A ULA Vulcan rocket failed about ten minutes after liftoff Sunday and 40 Amazon Leo satellites were lost.
claims.episode_span: destroyed 40 satellites for Amazon’s Leo internet network
claims.source_title: Amazon loses 40 Leo satellites in ULA Vulcan launch failure
claims.supporting_quote: A United Launch Alliance Vulcan rocket malfunctioned about 10 minutes after liftoff Sunday and failed to reach orbit, losing 40 satellites for Amazon Leo

claims.claim: The failure was ULA’s first total mission failure since the joint venture was formed in 2006.
claims.episode_span: first total mission failure since the Boeing–Lockheed Martin joint venture was formed in 2006
claims.source_title: Amazon loses 40 Leo satellites in ULA Vulcan launch failure
claims.supporting_quote: It was ULAs first total mission failure since the Boeing–Lockheed Martin joint venture was formed in 2006, Spaceflight Now reported.

claims.claim: Sunday’s flight was the first of 38 Vulcan launches Amazon purchased.
claims.episode_span: the first of 38 Vulcan launches Amazon has purchased
claims.source_title: Amazon loses 40 Leo satellites in ULA Vulcan launch failure
claims.supporting_quote: The flight was Vulcans first in nine months, and the first of 38 Vulcan launches that Amazon has purchased.

claims.claim: ULA said it does not yet have specific data on the cause.
claims.episode_span: ULA said it does not yet have specific data on what went wrong
claims.source_title: Amazon loses 40 Leo satellites in ULA Vulcan launch failure
claims.supporting_quote: ULA said it doesnt yet have specific data on what went wrong, and that it will work with Amazon and others to find the cause and return to flight as quickly as possible.

claims.claim: Amazon had said the second Vulcan mission could fly within weeks of the first.
claims.episode_span: Amazon had said a second Vulcan mission could fly within weeks
claims.source_title: Amazon loses 40 Leo satellites in ULA Vulcan launch failure
claims.supporting_quote: Amazon had said the second Vulcan mission could fly within weeks of the first.

claims.claim: Apple launched the Apple Health AI Usage Study in the US with OpenEvidence.

claims.supporting_quote: Yesterday, Apple announced the launch of the Apple Health AI Usage Study in the US, a virtual research study and associated app designed to advance the understanding of how people interact with conversational health AI tools.

claims.source_title: Apple announces the launch of the Apple Health AI Usage Study
claims.supporting_quote: To join, participants must have an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone (iPhone 15 Pro or later) running iOS 26 or later.

claims.claim: Study data will not be used to train AI models, and OpenEvidence deletes query and response data after 24 hours.
